metadata.title: Resolving the high-redshift JWST early galaxy and supermassive black hole crisis via chronodynamic proper time dilation
metadata.description: Spectroscopic discoveries by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) have precipitated an acute crisis for standard Lambda-CDM cosmology: the detection of massive, luminous galaxies (M_star > 10^10 to 10^11 M_sun) and overmassive supermassive black holes (M_BH > 10^7 to 10^9 M_sun) at redshifts z = 8 to 14, within the first 300-600 Myr after the Big Bang. Under standard Lambda-CDM, the available cosmological time is insufficient for standard hierarchical halo assembly and Eddington-limited black hole accretion. We show that Chronodynamic Relativity resolves this anomaly naturally through metric clock rate dilation eta(z) = (1+z)^(-n/2) (n = 3/4pi approx 0.2387). Because the metric clock ran faster in the early universe, the cumulative proper physical time elapsed between z = 14.32 and the present is expanded by +4.98x (Delta tau approx 1,424 Myr elapsed compared to 286 Myr in Lambda-CDM). This extended physical maturation window allows standard star formation rates and sub-Eddington accretion to build galaxies like JADES-GS-z14-0, GN-z11, and UHZ1 without requiring extreme initial conditions, super-Eddington accretion, or massive direct-collapse seeds.
